subject: Maths
title: Percentage increase and decrease
subtitle: Percentages · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can increase or decrease an amount by a given percentage using a multiplier.

key_vocab.definition: A percentage increase makes an amount larger. A percentage decrease makes it smaller. Use a single multiplier for efficiency.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can increase or decrease an amount by a given percentage using a multiplier.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Percentage increase and decrease -- A percentage increase makes an amount larger. A percentage decrease makes it smaller. Use a single multiplier for efficiency.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
To increase, add the percentage to 100% to get the multiplier. To decrease, subtract from 100%.
New = Original × multiplier
Increase: 1 + &frac{%}{100}. Decrease: 1 - &frac{%}{100}

Key examples:
  ✓ Increase £80 by 25%: 80 × 1.25 = £100  (multiplier 1.25)
  ✓ Decrease £60 by 10%: 60 × 0.90 = £54  (multiplier 0.90)
  ✓ VAT at 20%: multiply by 1.20  (adding 20%)
  ✗ Increase by 25% then decrease by 25% = original  (does not return to original)
  ✗ Decrease by 10%: multiply by 0.10  (that finds 10%, not 90%)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – percentage increase
  Increase £240 by 15%
  Multiplier = 1 + 0.15 = 1.15
  240 × 1.15
  = £276
  = £276
  (The multiplier 1.15 means 100% + 15% = 115% of original.)

Example 2 – percentage decrease
  Decrease £350 by 20%
  Multiplier = 1 - 0.20 = 0.80
  350 × 0.80
  = £280
  = £280
  (0.80 means keeping 80% (removing 20%).)

sections.title: Percentage increases
sections.content:
Increase each amount by the given percentage.

(a) £200 by 10%
(b) £450 by 20%
(c) £80 by 25%
(d) £1200 by 5%

sections.title: Percentage decreases
sections.content:
Decrease each amount by the given percentage.

(a) £300 by 10%
(b) £560 by 25%
(c) £90 by 30%
(d) £1500 by 15%

sections.title: Finding the multiplier
sections.content:
Write the single multiplier for each change.

(a) Increase by 35%
(b) Decrease by 12%
(c) Increase by 7.5%
(d) Decrease by 42%

sections.title: Reverse percentage problems
sections.content:
Find the original amount.

(a) After 20% increase, price = £480. Original?
(b) After 10% decrease, value = £540. Original?
(c) After 25% increase, bill = £75. Original?
(d) After 15% decrease, weight = £170. Original?

sections.title: Mixed percentage changes
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) £640 increased by 12.5%
(b) £880 decreased by 35%
(c) After 30% off, a coat costs £56. Original price?
(d) A house worth £250000 increases by 8%. New value?
(e) A salary of £32000 gets a 4.5% rise. New salary?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To increase by 15%, multiply by 1.15
✗ To decrease by 20%, multiply by 0.20
✗ A 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease gives the original
✓ To find original after increase, divide by the multiplier
✓ Decrease by 30% means multiplier is 0.70
